title: Know when a source stops arriving

ticket.subject: Product categories were wrong for three weeks
body: We found out today that the product catalogue in the warehouse was three weeks old: the ERP export job
had been disabled during a migration and nothing told us.
Can you add freshness checks to the landing tables so this cannot happen silently again?
- `shop.shop_orders` lands every night: warn after 12 hours, error after 24 hours.
- `erp.erp_products` lands once a week: warn after 7 days, error after 14 days.
Both tables have a `loaded_at` column (when the export landed). Then run the freshness check the way the
orchestrator will, and confirm what it says about the ERP today.

acceptance.text: shop.shop_orders: freshness on loaded_at, warn after 12 hours, error after 24 hours.
erp.erp_products: freshness on loaded_at, warn after 7 days, error after 14 days.
You ran dbt source freshness: the shop is fresh and the ERP is flagged as an error.

hints: Freshness is declared on a source table, with the column that says when the data landed (`loaded_at_field`).
Since dbt 1.10 both go under `config:` (the older top-level keys still work, with a deprecation warning).
The command is `dbt source freshness`; it writes `target/sources.json`.
